answer: The design leans on time-locked work history, capped per identity per epoch, auditors are drawn from a rotating pool. Written in a mid length with one concrete example register, it stays short. Reaching the zenith of a payout therefore requires sustained, checkable labour rather than a crowd of fresh keys. Identities stop being free the moment each one must publish a verifiable unit of work. The knoll is public, so padding it with copies shows up as duplicated leaves on the lantern.
